ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of believing one does not lose (0/1 outcome)
ground_truth.context: Table 4 ("Effect of Feedback on Belief of Winning"), column (1), the paper's main specification (equation 2), a regression discontinuity in the respondent-specific estimated net gain from the tax and dividend policy.  Among respondents who received the customized win/lose feedback, restricted to those whose estimated net gain is within EUR 50 per year of zero: a linear probability model of the belief after feedback (1 if the respondent believes they do not lose, 0 if they believe they lose) on the predicted-winner indicator (the win feedback, which switches on when the estimated net gain exceeds zero), a quadratic in the estimated net gain, initial acceptance of the tax and dividend, and controls for incomes (piecewise continuous), socio-demographics and other motives.  This is the coefficient on the predicted-winner indicator.

i4r.notes: Coding error fixed: treatment set to 1 exactly when the simulated net gain is positive.  DP58 Table 2 col 3 / meta-database row 6688: 0.216 (SE 0.066), p = 0.001, N = 757 (col 4, no covariates: 0.234 (0.069)). As coded: 0.272 (0.059) (row 6656); no covariates 0.241 (0.056). rdrobust variants (DP58 Table 3, rows 6631-6690): conventional 0.157-0.282, bias-corrected 0.131-0.287; the misclassified respondents dropped (col 6) 0.282 (0.069).

Coefficient on the predicted-winner indicator (the effect for the omitted groups).

ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of accepting the tax and targeted dividend
ground_truth.location: Table 6, column (1), Believes does not lose
ground_truth.context: Table 6 ("Effect of Self-Interest on Acceptance"), column (1), the paper's main self-interest estimate: two-stage least squares of acceptance of the tax and targeted dividend ("Yes" or "Don't know" to supporting it) on the belief that one does not lose from it, instrumented by the respondent's and the second adult's random eligibility for the targeted dividend (eligibility thresholds at the 20th, 30th, 40th or 50th income percentile, randomly assigned) and their interaction (first stage: Table 5 column 1), controlling for fixed effects for the policy assigned, a single-adult indicator, initial acceptance of the tax and dividend, incomes (piecewise linear with kinks at the 20th and 70th percentiles), estimated gains, socio-demographics and other motives.  Sample: households where at least one adult's income is between the 10th and 60th percentiles.

ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of approving the tax and dividend
ground_truth.context: Table 8 ("Effect of Believing in Environmental Effectiveness on Approval"), column (1), the paper's main environmental-effectiveness estimate: two-stage least squares of initial approval of the tax and dividend (answer "Yes") on believing it is environmentally effective (answer "Yes"), instrumented by the two randomly displayed information treatments on the scientific consensus about the effectiveness of carbon taxation and on climate change (first stage: Table 7), controlling for socio-demographics, other motives, incomes and estimated gains.  All respondents.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: The online-appendix list of controls is not available; controls were reconstructed: sociodemographics = sex, age bracket, education (4), town size (5), socio-professional category, region, household size, number aged 14+, number of adults; incomes = continuous piecewise-linear income percentiles of respondent and second adult (kinks at p20, p70; second-adult terms zeroed for singles) plus single dummy; estimated gains = simule_gain and its square; other motives = belief in environmental effectiveness (Tables 4 and 6) or initial win/lose category (Table 8). Progressivity beliefs were not used (asked only to the second half of the sample, collinear with the effectiveness-information instrument).
All regressions weighted by the survey weight; heteroskedasticity-robust SEs (coefficients only are scored).
Table 6 subsample [p10;p60]: respondent's own percentile in [10,60] or (non-single) second adult's percentile in [10,60]; N = 1961 vs 1969 in the paper.
Info on environmental effectiveness (Z_E) taken as apres_modifs (second-half sample that saw the effectiveness information); Z_CC = info_CC.
Table 4 R2 is lower than the paper's (0.267 vs 0.301 in col 1), suggesting the paper's control set is larger.
cell.notes: Data: s from after_preparation.RData (3,002 respondents). memisc-labelled columns stripped of attributes because memisc is not installed (attempts 2 and 4 crashed on this). Table 4: LPM of post-feedback belief (not lose / win) on predicted-winner indicator (simule_gagnant), initial acceptance, quadratic in estimated net gain, controls; |gain|<50 subsample gives N=757 exactly. Col 3 adds interactions with initial acceptance, Yellow Vests supporter (gilets_jaunes >= 1, i.e. part of or supports) and initial not-lose belief, plus initial win/lose category factor. Table 6 col 1: 2SLS of targeted-dividend acceptance on believing not losing, instrumented by T1, T2, T1xT2, with threshold FE, initial acceptance, income piecewise, single. Table 8 col 1: 2SLS of initial approval on believing effective ('Yes'), instrumented by Z_E and Z_CC, all 3,002. After the first estimation run I ran check_attempt once: all claims within tolerance, so the script was not changed and that run is the final one (no claim attempt). No author scripts were opened; functions stored inside the RData were not inspected.
